value.agency: Utah Department of Health and Human Services (plan review and operating permits delegated to local health departments)
value.pool_rule: Utah Admin. Code R392-302 (Design, Construction and Operation of Public Pools)
value.licensing: Contractor: Utah DOPL S330 Landscape and Recreation Contractor covers "swimming pools, prefabricated pools, spas, decorative pools, tanks, fountains" (excludes electrical work, which an S330 may subcontract to an E200/E201 contractor). Electrical: DOPL licenses electrical contractors (E200 general, E201 residential) and electricians in five classes (apprentice, journeyman, master, residential journeyman, residential master) under Utah Code Title 58, Chapter 55. Permits: Building and electrical permits are issued by the local building department (Salt Lake City Building Services, 451 South State Street, Room 215, for SLC projects); public pools, spas and interactive water features also need local health department plan review before construction (Salt Lake County Health Department in SLC) and an operating permit from that department.
value.notes: Utah is the reference row: R392-302-41 requires filtering the whole IWF volume within 30 minutes ((9)(a)(i)), a collector tank holding at least 3 minutes of combined feature + filter flow ((9)(g)), an approved secondary disinfection system per R392-302-35(8) ((6)(b); UV listed in 35(7)(b), 99.9% Cryptosporidium inactivation), and an automated ORP and pH controller operating whenever open ((6)(a)). IWFs must also meet the Title 15A State Construction Code ((2)).

Permits: Building and electrical permits are issued by the local building department (Salt Lake City Building Services, 451 South State Street, Room 215, for SLC projects); public pools, spas and interactive water features also need local health department plan review before construction (Salt Lake County Health Department in SLC) and an operating permit from that department.
citations: https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title15A/Chapter2/C15A-2-S103_2025070120250507.html — Utah Code 15A-2-103(1)(g): "the 2023 edition of the National Electrical Code" (version effective 7/1/2025; unchanged in the 7/1/2026 version) (read 2026-11-01) ; https://le.utah.gov/Session/2025/bills/enrolled/HB0313.pdf — H.B. 313 (2025) changes "[2020] 2023 edition" of the NEC, "takes effect on July 1, 2025" (read 2026-11-01) ; https://www.slc.gov/buildingservices/wp-content/uploads/sites/9/2026/07/SLC-Design-Criteria-2024-IBC_IRC.pdf — SLC Building Services enforces "2023 National Electric Code" (read 2026-11-01)

https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title15A/Chapter2/C15A-2-S103_2026050620260701.html — Utah Code 15A-2-103(1)(a), version effective 7/1/2026: "the 2024 edition of the International Building Code, including Appendices C and J" (previously 2021, effective until 6/30/2026); enacted by H.B. 65 (2026), https://le.utah.gov/Session/2026/bills/enrolled/HB0065.pdf — "this bill takes effect July 1, 2026" (read 2026-11-01)

https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title15A/Chapter2/C15A-2-S103_2026050620260701.html — Utah Code 15A-2-103(1)(b): "the 2021 edition of the International Residential Code" (IRC stays 2021 in the 7/1/2026 version) (read 2026-11-01)

https://le.utah.gov/xcode/Title15A/Chapter2/C15A-2-S103_2026050620260701.html — 15A-2-103(1)(n), effective 7/1/2026: "the residential provisions of the 2024 edition of the International Swimming Pool and Spa Code" (was 2021 until 6/30/2026; only the residential provisions are adopted, so public/commercial pools fall under health-department rule R392-302 instead) (read 2026-11-01)

https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/utah/health/title-R392/rule-R392-302 — R392-302 section index (R392-302-1 to -43) and the definitions/authority sections read for this research show no Model Aquatic Health Code reference or adoption; searches found no Utah MAHC adoption statement (read 2026-11-01). Absence of evidence, not a positive statement by the state.

https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/utah/Utah-Admin-Code-R392-302-1 — rule "establishes minimum standards for the sanitation, design, construction, operation, and maintenance of public pools"; authority 26B-1-202, 26B-7-113, 26B-7-402 (read 2026-11-01)

https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/utah/Utah-Admin-Code-R392-302-41 — Special Purpose Pools: Interactive Water Features; defined in R392-302-3 as "a public-use indoor or outdoor installation such as a splash pad, spray pad, wet deck" (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/utah/Utah-Admin-Code-R392-302-3) (read 2026-11-01)

issues.title: Trough surge is close to the freeboard
issues.detail: Drain-back from the 45 ft discharge run raises the trough 1.9 in at shut-down against 2.4 in of freeboard (house rule: 1.25 × surge).
issues.fix_hint: Deepen the trough to 16 in, or add a check valve at the weir header.

issues.title: Workbook and physics disagree by 11% on friction
issues.detail: Darcy-Weisbach gives 7.9 ft on the discharge; the DOC-0049 Hazen-Williams figure is 7.1 ft.
issues.fix_hint: Usually fine at this size; review the fittings on the discharge.

issues.title: The pump is a generic estimate
issues.detail: Pick a model from the catalog before the package goes out.
issues.fix_hint: Pick a pump in the Pump room.

verdict.headline: Works, with two warnings to sign off.

schedules.label: Schedules: equipment, piping, fittings, structural, electrical, controls

steps: Shut off and disconnect the autofill
Lower the water below the returns and skimmers, or drain the basin
Drain pump p1: open the drain plugs, store them in the basket
Drain the filter, heater and strainers; open every equipment drain
Pull the underwater lights or confirm they are rated to stay in frozen water
Turn off and lock out the feature circuits; leave heat on in a heated room

startup: Fill the trough to the autofill line.
Prime the pump and open the suction valve.
Level the weir lip to ±1/16 in before the first run.
